claims.head: Airtight vs. leaky on the kill
claims.body: On the penalty kill, Anaheim is near the top of the league, but San Jose is one of the worst. Penalties should hurt the Sharks more than the Ducks. Anaheim’s penalty kill has been near the bottom of the league for years, though. These two hand each other plenty of power plays, so special teams should get a real say.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 29% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the second-lowest in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Igor Chernyshov is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 13 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Michael Misa has taken his spot beside Will Smith and Macklin Celebrini. That line has had 44% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 53:03 together, down from 60% with Chernyshov.
Kiefer Sherwood is out week to week (upper body injury) and missed their last game.
Alexander Wennberg returned in their last game after missing 2 games.
A.J. Greer is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 9 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.
Stian Solberg was added to the roster on Nov 21.

stakes: The Sharks go in fourth in the Pacific with 22 points, a point behind the Ducks, third. A regulation win for the Sharks would lift them past the Ducks.

ANA.body: Anaheim has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Sharks’ way back in is getting good looks.

SJS.head: A tough matchup for the Sharks
SJS.body: Anaheim has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Sharks can pull it off if they get good looks.

story.head: Trouba returns to Anaheim
paras: The Sharks (10-12-2) lost 5-2 to Calgary on Nov 17, and the Ducks (11-11-1) lost 4-0 to Colorado on Thursday. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Sharks fourth (tied for 20th in the NHL) and the Ducks third (19th). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.
The Sharks’ record (.458) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.399), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Ducks’ record (.500) is about what their chances are worth.

The Sharks do a lot of their shooting from distance (2nd lowest) and ice the puck a lot (32nd). The Ducks play fast, open games (4th), give up a lot of dangerous shots (31st) and have had shaky goaltending (30th). Anaheim has allowed 3.87 goals a game, the third most in the league. The Ducks are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Sharks. On top of that, both teams like to hit, especially the Sharks (2nd), so expect plenty of it.

Macklin Celebrini (9 G / 18 A / 27 P in 22 GP) leads the Sharks in scoring, and Will Smith (8 G / 11 A / 19 P in 24 GP) is next in line. Cutter Gauthier (21 G / 8 A / 29 P in 22 GP) leads the Ducks in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. Leo Carlsson (6 G / 22 A / 28 P in 23 GP) isn’t far behind.

Yaroslav Askarov (6-9-1 / .888 SV% in 16 GS) will likely start for San Jose. Anaheim has two options in net: Laurent Brossoit (4-1-0 / .866 SV% in 5 GS) and Lukáš Dostál (4-6-1 / .857 SV% in 12 GS). Brossoit has started five of their last ten games, but Dostál got the last one on Thursday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
